name: the meadows
title: Open Meadows
description: Long grass to the knee, moving in waves under the wind. The sea is behind the cliff now, only a hush.
Open grass as far as the next hill, bending in the wind. Behind you, the cliff hides the sea.
Grass, waist-high in places, silver where the wind combs it. The sea is a murmur behind the cliff.
_map: position on the route map (grid cells); the camp (travelHours 0) has a path to every place

log: Bushes dot the slope ahead. Further down, a line of willows bends as if over water.
Low bushes stand in the grass, and further down, willows lean the way trees lean over water.
Here and there a dark bush in the grass. Lower down, a line of willows.

_arrive: what you see each time you come back: every line whose 'when' holds, in order

text: The grass again, and the wind in it.
Back in the long grass. The wind combs it flat.
The meadows open out again, bright after the cliff path.
Open sky again, and grass to the knee.
The meadows at night: grass hissing in the dark, no shape to anything.
In the dark the grass is only a sound around your legs.
Night over the grass. Somewhere, crickets.
The berry bushes are still heavy with fruit.
Dark berries on the bushes, waiting.
The bushes, still full of berries.
Below, the river runs under the willows.
You hear the river before you see it.
The river is still there, quick and clear.
The corn is ripe in the field.
The corn stands tall and ripe.

explore.name: look around
explore._explore: look around: a pop-up with what you see (view lines whose 'when' holds) and the landmarks not explored yet; no time passes until you pick one

text: Long grass rolls away inland, bending under the wind.
Grass to the knee, all the way to the next low hill.
Open meadows, silver-green, moving like water.

view.text: Dark bushes stand here and there in the grass.
The berry bushes, dark with fruit.
Lower down, a line of willows.
Near the river the ground lies flat.
Taller stalks stand out of the grass here and there.
Past the bushes, a humming in the flowers.

landmarks.label: the bushes
text: The bushes are heavy with small dark berries. You try one: sour, then sweet. Food, if you pick enough.
Close up, the bushes are full of berries, dark and soft. One tastes sharp and sweet. You could pick them.
Berries, hundreds of them, small and nearly black. Sour at first, then sweet. Worth picking.

landmarks.label: the willows
text: Under the willows runs a river, quick and clear over stones. You drink, and it is sweet. In the slow pools, fish hang in the current. With a spear you might take one.
The willows lean over a clear river. The water is cold and good to drink. Where it slows, fish hold still against the current. A spear could reach them.
A river, hidden by the willows: clear, cold, drinkable. In the deep bends, fish turn slowly. Too quick for hands, but not for a spear.

landmarks.label: the flat ground
text: Near the river the ground is flat and dark, the grass soft. Good earth. With a hoe, a field could grow here.
A flat stretch by the river, deep soil under the grass. A field would do well here, if you could break the ground.
Level ground near the water, black soil when you dig your fingers in. A place for a field.

landmarks.label: the tall seed heads
text: Among the grass, taller stalks with thin ears: wild corn. Small, but you could eat it. Or sow it.
Wild corn grows in a patch of tall stalks, small ears hidden in the leaves. Food, and seed.
Tall stalks with little ears of corn, gone wild. Enough to eat a little, or to sow.

landmarks.label: the humming
text: Bees, working the flowers past the bushes. Wild ones, nesting somewhere. A hollow log might bring them to you.
The humming is bees, hundreds of them, in the flowers. Give them a hollow log and they might stay.
A swarm of wild bees in the flowers. A hive would keep them, and their honey.

activities.name: pick berries
log: Your fingers come away purple.
You strip the bushes branch by branch.
Berries, a handful at a time. Thorns catch your sleeves.
You fill your hands, then your pockets.
Small dark berries, soft enough to bruise.

activities.name: drink water
log: You kneel at the river and drink. Cold and sweet.
River water, cold enough to ache.
You drink from your hands, the current pulling at your fingers.
The river tastes of stone and grass.

activities.name: catch fish

text: Two fish, flapping in the grass.
Two fish from the same pool.
Two fish, silver and cold.
One fish. It will do.
One fish, flapping on the bank.
A single fish, heavy for its size.
Nothing. The current carries them off.
Nothing. They slip back into the deep water.
The spear comes up with weed, nothing else.

log: You stand on a stone above a slow pool, spear raised.
You wade into the river to your knees and wait.
Under the willows you wait for a fish to hold still.

activities.name: cut willow twigs
log: You cut long, supple twigs from the willows.
Willow twigs, green and bending, an armful.
You strip the willows of their long whips.

activities.name: gather corn
log: You search the tall grass for the ears of wild corn.
A few small ears among the grass.
Wild corn, thin ears, hard kernels.

activities.name: twist cord
log: You twist long grass into cord, strand over strand.
Grass, rolled and twisted on your thigh into cord.
A length of grass cord, rough but strong.
